name: Spoon
label: Matador
lede: Britt Daniel and Jim Eno made a $3,000 debut for Matador, got signed and dropped by Elektra inside a year, and wrote a single about the executive who did it. A decade of steady records on Merge later, Metacritic named Spoon its top artist of the 2000s.

eras.title: Named after a Can song
eras.text: Britt Daniel and Jim Eno met in an Austin rockabilly trio, then started a band named for a Can song. A $3,000 debut album got them to New York's Matador Records.

years.h: Two Austin rockabilly players name a band after a Can song
years.p: Daniel and Eno meet in the trio The Alien Beats. With Greg Wilson on guitar and Andy Maguire on bass, they take the name from Can's Spoon.
years.xp: Daniel, born in Galveston and raised in Temple, Texas, had already been through the high school band the Zygotes and a UT Austin band called Skellington. He had worked as a sound designer and composer for the game company Origin Systems.

years.h: Spoon's first record is a vinyl EP called Nefarious
years.p: Daniel is also putting out experimental music as Drake Tungsten.

years.cap: Britt Daniel on an early East Coast trip, 1995
years.h: $3,000 and a converted garage get Spoon onto Matador
years.p: Producer John Croslin, who briefly plays bass in Spoon in 1996, records Telephono at home. Matador signs the band the same year.
years.xp: The studio was Croslin's garage, called Dogland. He recorded to eight-track tape, sessions ran in the evenings after his shift at Half Price Books, and his idea was to mix every song's eight tracks down to two to leave room for overdubs.

eras.title: The Pixies problem
eras.text: Matador put out the debut to reviews that kept saying Pixies. The bass chair turned over again and again, and by 1997 Daniel had decided Matador thought his band was too commercial.

years.h: Reviewers hear the Pixies all over Telephono
years.p: Texas Monthly puts first-year sales at about 1,300 copies. The same piece quotes Daniel: "we thought [Telephono] was going to go over like gangbusters."
years.xp:
Rolling Stone gave the record two stars, called it "engaging" and "memorable", and accused the band of plagiarizing the Pixies, per Texas Monthly.

Matador co-owner Gerard Cosloy later described it as "a building block on the way to Spoon becoming a fixture in every North American coffeehouse."

years.h: After Andy Maguire leaves, the bass job changes hands three times
years.p: John Croslin, Hunter Darby and Scott 'Clanky' Adair each hold it before the end of 1997.

years.src: Texas Monthly · Wikipedia: A Series of Sneaks
years.h: Soft Effects strips Spoon down to bones
years.p: Matador's second Spoon release shows the clipped, minimalist style that becomes Daniel's signature.
years.xp: It didn't help the label's case. Texas Monthly says the EP "was all but ignored."

years.h: Joshua Zarbo sees Spoon at the Argo in Denton, then auditions
years.p: He takes the bass for the next nine years.

years.h: Spoon walks away from Matador for Elektra
years.p: Daniel feels Matador sees Spoon as too commercial. Elektra's Ron Laffitte has chased the band for over a year, and Spoon agrees to go.

eras.title: The agony of Laffitte
eras.text: Elektra kept Spoon for about one album. The executive who signed the band left, the label dropped it that week, and Daniel answered with a single named after him.

years.h: A Series of Sneaks is out of print within a year
years.p: Spoon signs to Elektra in February and recorded the album across six Austin studios in 1997. By January 1999 it is gone from the racks.

years.h: Elektra drops Spoon the week Ron Laffitte leaves
years.p: Laffitte chased the band for a year, stopped returning calls once they signed, and was gone shortly after release. Spoon is dropped about four months after the album.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Laffitte quit that week and the band was dropped from the label. The record had been mostly finished before the label move, so Elektra bought a finished album and let it disappear.

Daniel later compared its sales unfavourably with a single week of the next album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Spoon · Wikipedia: Kill the Moonlight
years.h: Daniel answers Laffitte with a two-song single
years.p: The Agony of Laffitte and Laffitte Don't Fail Me Now come out on Omaha's Saddle Creek Records.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls it a vindictive yet humorously titled two-song concept single. Merge reissued A Series of Sneaks in 2002 with both songs as bonus tracks.

years.h: Daniel temps in New York while Eno designs chips in Austin
years.p: The 10-song album is done by May. Labels reject the demos week after week.
years.xp: Producer Mike McCarthy and Matador's [[Gerard Cosloy|b3c600d5-e1dd-4525-855d-6d4f950c3be6]] showed interest. McCarthy reworked the record, cut songs aimed at the old A&R man and added three new ones, and Daniel called it the hardest album to make.

eras.title: Merge, and the long way up
eras.text: Merge Records in North Carolina became home. Each record sold more than the last, and a piano song from Kill the Moonlight started turning up on television.

years.h: Love Ways is Spoon's first record for Merge
years.p: Zarbo sits it out; he was temporarily away.

yt: Everything Hits at Once, official video
years.h: Girls Can Tell outsells both earlier albums combined
years.p: Britt Daniel on the first week, which came close to everything A Series of Sneaks had sold.
years.xp: By 2009 the album was just under 100,000. Daniel names the Kinks, the Supremes and Elvis Costello's Get Happy!!, borrowed from Eleanor Friedberger, as influences.

yt: The Way We Get By, official video
years.h: Kill the Moonlight: tambourine, piano and space
years.p: Made with Mike McCarthy in Austin, it becomes one of Merge's biggest records. The Way We Get By lands in The O.C. and later Stranger than Fiction.
years.xp: Merge also reissued A Series of Sneaks in 2002 with both Laffitte songs as bonus tracks. Kill the Moonlight had sold around 153,000 by December 2009.

eras.title: Top artist of the decade
eras.text: Each Spoon album from Gimme Fiction to Transference opened higher than the one before, and the reviews stayed high. By 2010 the band had played Saturday Night Live and cracked the Billboard top five.

years.h: Gimme Fiction opens at No. 44 on the Billboard 200
years.p: Merge releases it in the US and Matador in Europe.

years.h: Daniel scores Stranger than Fiction, and Rob Pope takes bass
years.p: Daniel arranges the film's music with Brian Reitzell, mostly from Spoon songs. Pope replaces Zarbo.

years.h: Ga Ga Ga Ga Ga debuts at No. 10
years.p: The band promotes its sixth album on Letterman, Conan and Austin City Limits.

years.cap: Spoon at Gage Park, Hamilton, Ontario, August 2007
years.h: Spoon plays The Underdog and You Got Yr. Cherry Bomb on SNL
years.p: Musical guest on the October 6 episode, three months after Ga Ga Ga Ga Ga arrives at No. 10.

years.cap: Spoon at the Astor Theatre, Perth
years.h: Metacritic ranks Spoon first of the 2000s
years.p: Based on review scores from 2000 to 2009, no act rated better.

years.h: Transference opens at No. 4 on 53,000 copies
years.p: That April, Spoon guests on Conan O'Brien's Legally Prohibited tour in Eugene, Oregon.

eras.title: Home to Matador
eras.text: Daniel took a side trip with a new band, then Spoon left Merge after five records. Two albums later it was back on Matador, the label it walked away from in 1997.

years.h: Daniel starts Divine Fits with Dan Boeckner
years.p: Daniel forms [[Divine Fits|0cc883bb-a8a5-4b8a-ba5c-ab4e6b9afc09]] with [[Wolf Parade|b7ddce8b-9e5c-46bd-9d33-41b134ce1a7f]]'s [[Dan Boeckner|142c1d98-df0e-4df5-b202-e63814693024]] and a member of [[New Bomb Turks|013d71e5-ecb2-486a-bd82-6e7d9129acfc]]. It runs until 2013.

years.h: They Want My Soul is Spoon's first record off Merge
years.p: Joe Chiccarelli and Dave Fridmann produce it for Loma Vista. Pitchfork calls it the quintet's most booming record.

years.h: Spoon returns to Matador with Hot Thoughts after 21 years
years.p: The ninth album is its first Matador release since Telephono in 1996. Eric Harvey leaves that year.

years.big: "So this guy can just do anyone's job, huh."
years.h: Pete Buttigieg plays The Way We Get By on piano
years.p: Presidential candidate Pete Buttigieg is filmed playing Spoon's The Way We Get By on piano before a campaign event. That is Spoon's reply on social media.

years.cap: Spoon at Piknik i Parken, Oslo
years.h: Rob Pope leaves after 13 years on bass
years.p: He announces his exit weeks before Matador's best-of, Everything Hits at Once, comes out on July 26.

eras.title: Thirty years to a Grammy nod
eras.text: A pandemic held up the tenth album, which then earned Spoon its first Grammy nomination nearly three decades in. The band keeps touring with peers it came up with.

years.h: Spoon covers Tom Petty while the finished album waits
years.p: Breakdown and A Face in the Crowd come out as the pandemic holds up the record.

years.cap: Spoon at First Avenue, Minneapolis, April 24, 2022
years.h: Nearly three decades in, Spoon gets its first Grammy nod
years.p: Lucifer on the Sofa, recorded at Jim Eno's studio from late 2018, is nominated in November for Best Rock Album. Adrian Sherwood remixes it as Lucifer on the Moon.
years.xp: The nomination, at the 65th Annual Grammy Awards, is the band's first. The album itself came out in February 2022.

years.h: Spoon books a tour with Pixies and previews an 11th album
years.p: Chateau Blues and Guess I'm Fallin In Love come out first. In June 2026 Spoon co-headlines with [[The Beths|4c74fc48-8108-4556-87af-154af74f2ce5]].

sources.title: Texas Monthly: Thirty Years Ago, Spoon's First Album Changed My Life
